title: Add per-route/per-tier SLOs + burn-rate alerts (enterprise lanes)
author: Aisha Bello
description:
Context: Hot-route capacity protection introduces tier-aware admission control + enterprise lanes in routing. To keep this operationally safe, we need SLOs and burn-rate alerts that can be sliced by (route, tier) without blowing up cardinality.

This PR adds:
- SLO definitions for a curated set of "enterprise hot routes" with explicit per-tier objectives (enterprise vs self_serve) and separate error-budget policies.
- Burn-rate alert rules (multi-window) for each enterprise hot route, with alert labels that map cleanly to incident routing.
- A small generator + validation that enforces label/cardinality constraints (route must be from an allowlist; tier must be one of {enterprise,self_serve}; region is optional and default-off).
- Documentation and examples for wiring lane-specific SLO reporting to the gateway/router metrics.

Non-goals:
- No changes to runtime scheduling SLOs.
- No dashboards in this repo (dashboards are handled in observability-pack PR-922); this only defines the SLO + alert primitives consumed downstream.

Motivation: During partial fleet degradation/regional dips, we want a clean signal for whether enterprise routes stayed within contract SLOs even if we intentionally shed lower-tier traffic (429s / over-capacity) to protect the fleet.

Implementation details:
- Uses existing slo-toolkit schema v3 (service-level SLO objects) and adds a new "slo_group" convention: hot_route/<route_group>/tier/<tier>.
- Error query counts only "served" requests for latency SLOs and treats deliberate throttling as excluded from availability, per ADR-0148 semantics (the gateway/router must emit reason_code=over_capacity and status=429).
- Availability SLO is measured as success / (success + 5xx + timeouts). 429 over_capacity is excluded for enterprise tier SLOs, but still tracked separately via a supplemental indicator.

Example (generated) SLO entry:
name: hosted-api.hot-route.chat_completions.enterprise.availability
service: hosted-api
objective: 99.95
labels: {route_group: "chat_completions", tier: "enterprise"}

Alerting:
- Page: 2% / 1h and 5% / 6h burn for enterprise tier (only)
- Ticket: 1% / 6h and 2% / 24h burn for enterprise tier
- Self-serve tier only gets ticket alerts (no page) for now.

Rollout note: these SLOs assume the gateway/router emits route_group and tier labels per the hot-route capacity protection instrumentation. If those labels are missing, the generator will fail validation (to prevent silently creating an always-green SLO).

Related:
- ENG-4827 (metrics + cardinality safety)
- ENG-4824 (priority lanes) / ENG-4826 (reason codes, Retry-After)
- observability-pack PR-922 (dashboards + alert routing)
commits: slo-schema: add route_group/tier constraints + docs for hot route SLO groups
redwood/hosted-api: add enterprise hot routes SLO definitions (availability + latency)
alerts: add burn-rate alert templates for enterprise hot routes
validation: fail if required labels missing or allowlist violated
docs: clarify 429 over_capacity accounting and reason_code expectations
review_conversation:
Sean Gallagher: For the availability indicator, can we confirm 429 over_capacity is excluded only for enterprise tier? I want to avoid masking self-serve brownouts.
Aisha Bello: Yep. Enterprise tier excludes 429 over_capacity from availability, but we still emit a supplemental indicator/alert metric. Self_serve availability keeps 429 excluded as well? (current draft excluded for both) — I can adjust.
Aisha Bello (follow-up): Updated so only enterprise excludes 429 over_capacity from availability; self_serve counts 429 as "bad" for availability but does not page. Added a note in docs + changelog.

Allison Grant: Cardinality: route_group is ok but only if it’s allowlisted. Can you enforce a hard max in validation so we don’t accidentally add 200 groups later?
Aisha Bello: Added validator: route_group must be in hot_route_allowlist.yaml; generator errors if allowlist size > 50 unless override flag is set (and override is blocked in CI).

Sergio Costa: Alert labels: please add "paging_team" and "runbook" labels for enterprise page alerts so incident-bot can enrich the page.
Aisha Bello: Done. Added paging_team=eng-oncall and runbook link to overload-throttling-and-priority-routing-response (Confluence) for enterprise-tier burn-rate pages.

Mina Haddad: The SLO queries assume tier label is present on router metrics. Are we standardizing on tier vs lane? Router uses lane=enterprise right now.
Aisha Bello: Good catch. I updated queries to accept either tier or lane, but normalize to tier via relabel in recording rules. Added a validation test to ensure at least one is present.

Sean Gallagher: Looks good after the self_serve change. Please ensure page alerts are only enterprise tier.
Aisha Bello: Confirmed. Page alerts match tier="enterprise" only; self_serve is ticket-only.

Allison Grant: Approved.
Sergio Costa: Approved.
Sean Gallagher: Approved.
release_notes: Adds enterprise hot-route per-tier SLO definitions and burn-rate alert rules consumed by downstream alert routing/dashboards. Enterprise tier gets paging burn-rate alerts; self-serve tier is ticket-only. Enforces allowlisted route_group to keep metric cardinality bounded.
